summary_hint: <debtor(s)> filed Chapter <bankruptcy_chapter> bankruptcy on <filing_date> in <court> (case <case_number>); debts primarily <consumer/business>, amended <yes/no>.

typed_core.name: debtor_1_legal_name
typed_core.why: identity: the primary filer; matches to the borrower

typed_core.name: debtor_2_legal_name
typed_core.why: identity: joint filer (spouse/co-borrower)

typed_core.name: ssn_or_itin_last4
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted, last-4): the debtor's SSN last-4 on the petition; MUST be typed, never catch-all
typed_core.prompt_hint: The petition carries SSN last-4 — file it in ssn_or_itin_last4 (and _2), NEVER the catch-all

typed_core.name: ssn_or_itin_last4_2
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted, last-4): joint debtor's SSN last-4

typed_core.name: debtor_address
typed_core.why: identity: the debtor address on the petition; identity/consistency

typed_core.name: county_of_residence
typed_core.why: identity / disambiguator: venue/residence context

typed_core.name: bankruptcy_court_name
typed_core.why: identity: the filing court — provenance/authenticity

typed_core.name: case_number
typed_core.why: PII (confidential) / identity: the case key that ties the filing to the discharge (#050) and to the credit-report public record

typed_core.name: bankruptcy_chapter
typed_core.why: disambiguator: Chapter 7 vs 11 vs 13 — drives the seasoning period and the meaning of the filing
typed_core.prompt_hint: The chapter is a load-bearing fact (seasoning context) — keep verbatim

typed_core.name: amended_filing_indicator
typed_core.why: disambiguator: whether this is an amended petition — which version governs
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish the amended petition from the original — the amended version governs

typed_core.name: filing_date
typed_core.why: processor: the petition date — the bankruptcy event date used for timeline/seasoning context
typed_core.prompt_hint: The filing date is a load-bearing fact (bankruptcy event date) — extract precisely; do NOT judge whether the bankruptcy is seasoned or disqualifying

typed_core.name: debts_primarily_consumer_or_business
typed_core.why: processor / disambiguator: consumer vs business debts — affects means test and how the bankruptcy is weighed
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture consumer vs business debt classification verbatim (the means-test selection)

typed_core.name: filing_basis_and_venue
typed_core.why: processor: the stated basis/venue — completeness of the filing profile

typed_core.name: estimated_asset_range
typed_core.why: processor: rough asset scale — context for the case

typed_core.name: estimated_liability_range
typed_core.why: processor: rough liability scale — context for the case

typed_core.name: rental_property_eviction_judgment
typed_core.why: processor: an eviction judgment on a rented residence signals housing-payment history risk

typed_core.name: attorney_name
typed_core.why: processor: representing counsel — an authenticity/verification contact

typed_core.name: document_issue_date
typed_core.why: processor: petition preparation date when distinct from filing_date

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity: links the filing to the loan file, when stated (confidential)

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity: subject/non-subject property when referenced

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date, document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: classified upstream; the petition is a standard federal form but no rule reads its form number here

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: the 'issuer' is the court/preparer; court captured by bankruptcy_court_name

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: redundant — the parties are the debtors (debtor_*)

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a petition's execution is the debtor/attorney signature, retained as debtor_signatures_and_dates/attorney_name where relevant; generic signature objects have no consumer

rejected.name: debtor_signatures_and_dates, attorney_or_preparer_signature
rejected.reason: execution details with no rule/processor consumer beyond confirming who filed; defer

rejected.name: other_names_used, business_names_and_eins, prior_bankruptcy_cases, pending_related_cases
rejected.reason: object[]/person_or_entity[] with no consumer today; defer to catch-all (business EINs would need a redactor if promoted)

rejected.name: estimated_creditor_count_range, funds_available_for_unsecured_creditors
rejected.reason: low-value case-profile detail with no consumer

encoding_variations: SSN presentation: petitions (official Form 101) show SSN as xxx-xx-1234 (last-4 only) — file under ssn_or_itin_last4; if a full SSN ever appears, it is still PII and must be typed
Chapter / amended: 'Chapter 7', 'Amended Voluntary Petition' — bankruptcy_chapter and amended_filing_indicator degrade to text; keep verbatim
Consumer vs business: the means-test checkbox — debts_primarily_consumer_or_business degrades to text; keep the exact selection
Ranges: assets/liabilities/creditors are stated as banded ranges ('$0–$50,000', '50–99 creditors') — estimated_asset_range / estimated_liability_range degrade to text as reported

open_questions.q: No rule consumes this document today (Tier 3, rule_count 0). The filing pairs with the discharge (#050) for seasoning.
open_questions.recommendation: keep those fields so a seasoning/means-test rule can be built without re-extraction

open_questions.q: Nested-list candidate — prior_bankruptcy_cases is the strongest repeating structure with mortgage relevance (multiple/serial bankruptcies affect eligibility).
options: promote to a flat-row nested list
open_questions.recommendation: defer until a multiple-bankruptcy rule exists; flag then

open_questions.q: business_names_and_eins PII — if promoted, EINs need masking (registered kind employer_ein).
options: promote and build with a redactor
open_questions.recommendation: keep deferred; if promoted, build with a redactor, never catch-all

open_questions.q: case_number PII treatment — same question as #050 (confidential, keys a public record).
options: register as a masked PII field
open_questions.recommendation: typed identity, unmasked, but flag for the privacy reviewer

open_questions.q: Multiple enums/bools degraded (chapter, amended, consumer/business, asset/liability ranges).

notes: The filing date and chapter are the load-bearing facts (bankruptcy event date + seasoning context).
Do NOT judge whether the bankruptcy is seasoned or disqualifying — capture the facts; rules/underwriters judge.

Ambiguity: case_number is tagged PII (confidential) but the design recommends keeping it as a typed identity field, unmasked — reason_class set to identity and pii left null pending the privacy reviewer (open question 4 blocks).
business_names_and_eins (deferred) would carry EINs; an EIN is a registered PII kind (employer_ein, masked). If promoted, it MUST be a typed/redacted field, never catch-all.
